item.title: Yellow rain warning announced for Co. Monaghan
item.description: Met Éireann has issued a status yellow rain warning for Co. Monaghan. The warning is valid from 3 a.m on Thursday, February 5th until Friday, February 6th at 3am. The national forecaster has advised that further rain falling on already saturated ground, combined with high river levels, could lead to localised flooding. item.description: A Lithuanian national who resides in Cavan Town has been remanded in custody following a drugs seizure worth an estimated value of €112,000. 48-year-old Alexsej Sergejev with an address of 40 St Clares Court, Cavan Town appeared before Monaghan District Court today and is charged with possession of drugs for sale or supply. item.title: Cavan man on ongoing IFA protest
item.description: A Cavan man says the ongoing IFA protest is not intimidating staff trying to enter the Bord Bia building. IFA protesters have been positioned outside the building for 10 days, before they made their way into the headquarters of Bord Bia yesterday afternoon. This is in relation to the calls for the resignation of Chairperson Larry Murrin, after it emerged that his company, Dawn Farms' imported Brazilian beef. item.title: Gardai appeal for information over Cavan burglaries
item.description: Gardai are appealing for information in relation to two burglaries in Cavan. Garda Lisa Stevens is appealing to anyone with information to come forward. Gardai in Cavan are investigating a burglary which occurred on the 12th of January between the hours 4pm and 6pm. Advertisement The incident was reported in the Mullaghboy area. item.title: Man further charged in relation to fatal Monaghan collision
item.description: A 56-year-old man has been further charged in relation to a fatal collision in Co Monaghan. Ion Bucurica previously appeared before Monaghan District Court in relation to dangerous driving causing the death of mother of two, Emma Mackeral. The Romanian national who resides in France appeared in front of Judge Raymond Finnegan today and was further charged with no insurance and failure to produce in court. item.title: Calls for Ballyhaise bus shelter reiterated
item.description: A local councillor says that Ballyhaise is calling out for a bus shelter. There is two separate local link routes that go through Ballyhaise, with a stop in the village, as well as two school buses. Stiofan Conaty says that this means there is potentially hundreds of people getting on and off the bus everyday. item.title: Co Cavan woman shares inspiring cancer journey to help others
item.description: A Co Cavan woman who overcame a cancerous tumour on her throat has shared her story on World Cancer Day to highlight the importance of getting yourself checked. Today marks World Cancer Day. The Irish Cancer Society is marking the event with a further commitment of over €1 million for the Young Onset Cancer Pilot Programme for this and next year, delivered in partnership with the Trinity St James’s Cancer Institute. item.title: Cavan man accused of murdering his mother to stand trial in April
item.description: A Cavan man who is accused of murdering his mother and attempting to murder his father will go on trial at the Central Criminal Court in Dublin in April. Danny Heyneman (32), with an address at Kilnavart, Ballyconnell in Co Cavan, is charged with the murder of Annie Heyneman and the attempted murder of Henk Heyneman at the family home in Kilnavart on January 11, 2025. The matter is listed for trial on April 13 next, with a mention date in the Central Criminal Court on February 18. Advertisement

item.title: Owners of EuroGiant chain enter liquidation
item.description: The High Court has today appointed liquidators to the companies which operate the EuroGiant chain across Ireland. The discount retailer has 77 stores across the country including in Cavan and Monaghan, employing around 640 staff on a national scale. These jobs are now under threat. EuroGeneral Limited and Bushgrove Limited have blamed "rising costs" for the decision.
